html:
Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa, north of the Zambezi. Britain ruled it as Northern Rhodesia from 1911 until independence in 1964.

Before colonial rule it held kingdoms such as the Lozi of the upper Zambezi floodplain and the Kazembe in the north. David Livingstone reached Victoria Falls in 1855. The British South Africa Company took control in the 1890s and ran the territory until 1924.

From the late 1920s copper mining built the Copperbelt, and copper has driven the economy ever since.

  • 1953 to 1963: part of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland.
  • 1964: independence under Kenneth Kaunda, who ruled a one-party state from 1972.
  • 1970 to 1975: China built the TAZARA Railway to Dar es Salaam, so copper could avoid white-ruled Rhodesia.
  • 1991: Kaunda lost the first multiparty election and stepped down.
sum: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa, north of the Zambezi. Britain ruled it as Northern Rhodesia from 1911 until independence in 1964.
